seen.extent: Viewed only Carta 1, Genoa 10 Nov 1496 (stamped '1496'): pp. 1-2 clear Spanish, then a spread (viewer page 3) with about 40 lines of continuous symbol cipher over two pages (about 20 lines per page). Letters 2-7 (to Nov 1522) not opened.
seen.cipher: Letter 1 carries a full-page-pair of a symbol/sign cipher (strokes, crosses, loops; not digits) written in long lines; zoomed: no interlinear or marginal plaintext and no decipherment bound with it, the cipher is not a show-through. Letters 2-7: whether and how they are ciphered is not checked.

seen.extent: Viewed one spread (viewer page 44, a Mirabel letter to Gondomar): about 4-5 lines of numeral cipher groups interlined in Spanish prose on the right leaf. Other ciphered letters in the 108 folios not individually located; the card summary says 'algunas cifradas'.
seen.cipher: Spanish ambassador's numeral nomenclator: groups of digits (two- and three-digit numbers, some with dots/marks) mixed with clear words (con, por, de) inside the text. No interlinear plaintext above the groups; a short marginal note on the left of the right leaf could be a contemporary clear (the coloma1622 notes treat marginal clears of this volume as a crib source, one margin on p.15 being only show-through). No decipherment is bound with it that I could confirm.
